title: Crucible Analytics - capacity decision workshop
meeting_header:
Date: 2027-02-16 16:30 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood Solutions), Dana Cole (Crucible CTO), Marcus Lee (Crucible Head of Infra), Priyanka Rao (Crucible Security), Evan Mills (Product)
summary: Discovery workshop to decide between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated reserved GPUs, or Private deployment. Covered traffic profiles, isolation/security requirements, burst patterns (conference weekends), cost targets, and pilot scope. Action items include sending pricing scenarios, security stack docs, and scheduling a short benchmark run with sample prompts.

reserved GPU sizing and burst strategy

transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE, joined by Priya our SE and Diego on solutions. Can we do quick intros?
[00:12] Dana: Yeah hi, I'm Dana, CTO at Crucible. We build analytics pipelines for retail pricing, want to add a natural language insights layer.
[00:18] Marcus: Marcus here, I run infra and ops. I'll focus on the deployment constraints.
[00:22] Priyanka: Priyanka, security, I'll ask the hard Qs.
[00:27] Samir: Great. High level - today we want to understand your traffic shape, isolation needs and decide whether hosted, dedicated reserved GPUs, or private makes sense. Priya, can you frame the typical tradeoffs?
[00:39] Priya (SE): Sure. Hosted is fastest to get started, pay as you go, we handle model updates and multi-tenant infra. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity - predictable throughput and isolation between your workloads and others, cheaper per-token at scale but commits required. Private (VPC / on-prem) gives the most control for compliance and data residency but longer lead times and ops burden. Important tradeoffs: latency SLOs, cost per 1k tokens, and how you want failover to work.
[01:05] Evan: Quick question — our bursty events are mostly weekend promotions and quarterly reporting days. We can spike maybe 6-8x baseline for several hours, sometimes short 10–20 minute microbursts. Does Redwood handle that gracefully?
[01:18] Priya (SE): Yes, with dedicated we support pre-warmed hot pools and burst capacity; you can define reserved baseline and configure burst guardrails. We do automatic fallback to hosted variants if the reserved pool is saturated, depending on policy. For private, you'd need capacity planning and static excess.
[01:34] Marcus: What about noisy neighbor risk? We have strict isolation needs for certain models that touch PII. Can dedicated guarantee isolation, or do we need private?
[01:44] Priya: Dedicated gives tenant isolation at the pool level — your workloads run on reserved nodes. There is still a soft multi-tenancy at control plane level for Hosted control plane, but runtime is in your pool. For strict regulatory needs where control plane separation is mandated, Private (VPC with customer-managed control plane or on-prem) is recommended.
[02:02] Dana: Our SLO goal is p95 token latency under 120ms for typical comple- uh, typical 256-token prompts. Cost target is a blended per-invocation price that doesn't exceed our current LM budget. We're sensitive to cold-starts for chat.
[02:18] Priya: Sounds reasonable. For 256-token prompts p95 120ms, we usually recommend model selection plus quantization and a warm pool. The runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching to reduce repeated context cost which helps for chat.
[02:33] Marcus: Can you explain pre-warm behavior? We don't want GPUs sitting idle but we need very fast warm-up when burst happens.
[02:40] Priya: Pre-warm is configurable. You can maintain a minimum number of warm instances (hot pool) and define pre-warm strategy — time-based, schedule-based (e.g., weekends), or predictive based on historical spikes. There's also a fast cold start path but it depends on model size and quantization. Pre-warm increases cost but reduces tail latency.
[02:58] Dana: For numbers — currently we average 75 req/s during weekdays, peaks to ~600 req/s for a few hours during promo weekends. Average tokens per request is ~180, peak concurrent requests hit 400–500 at spike. Does that map to reserved GPU counts?
[03:14] Priya: Rough back-of-envelope: depends on model. If you're using an open 7B-style model that's quantized and gives ~30 req/s per GPU at your average token length, you'd need ~3 GPUs baseline and additional 10–12 GPUs for spike capacity, plus headroom. For a 13B model those numbers change; we can model this precisely once we have your token distribution and exact model candidate.
[03:36] Marcus: We want clear fallback policies. If we reserve 6 GPUs and burst 10x, will traffic get rejected or routed to hosted?
[03:45] Priya: You set routing policy. Options: queue (with backpressure), overflow to hosted (best-effort compatibility if model variant exists), or autoscale within allowed burst cap. We recommend overflow-to-hosted with canary routing and rate-limits to protect quality.
[03:58] Evan: About model variants — say we run quantized 8-bit on dedicated but use a full-precision 16-bit on hosted fallback. How do you handle output parity?
[04:08] Diego: Diego here — we surface per-route model profiles and performance diffs. In practice, quantization can slightly alter logits; you should pin tests via eval prompt sets. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization levels by workload and warns on quality regressions and we can tie alerts to your eval set.
[04:26] Priyanka (Security): On encryption — does Redwood support customer-managed KMS for private and dedicated? We need key separation for production models.
[04:34] Priya (SE): Yes. For Private we support customer KMS/HSM and full key ownership. For Dedicated (hosted dedicated pools) we integrate with BYOK where possible; for some cloud providers there's an integration path. We'll share the security playbook.
[04:48] Priyanka (Security): And audit logs? Retention windows? We need at least 12 months of immutable audit logs for access and admin actions.
[04:56] Samir: We have plan tiers for log retention; 12 months is in our enterprise package. We'll attach the SOC2 and log retention docs.
[05:05] Marcus: Network — VPC peering or private link? We prefer private link to avoid routing through public internet.
[05:11] Priya (SE): We support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and on-prem connectors depending on the cloud. For Private deployments on-prem it's direct. We'll capture your cloud (you mentioned GCP?) and advise best fit.
[05:23] Dana: Yes GCP us-east region. Also some data residency concerns in EU for certain clients.
[05:29] Priya: We can place dedicated pools in region and handle routing by region. For EU residency we'd advise private deployment or a dedicated pool in the EU region, depending on SLA.
[05:38] Evan: Ok, what's the pilot look like? Minimal viable pilot to validate latency and cost.
[05:43] Samir: Typical pilot: 2-week benchmark with 3–4 reserved nodes mapped to realistic traffic from your trace, run against your prompt set and a Redwood-verified reference model. We'll measure p95/p99 latency, cost per token, cold-start behavior, and failover. Then we review results and iterate on sizing.
[06:00] Marcus: Are there minimum commitment windows for dedicated? We'd consider 6–12 months if the economics are right.
[06:05] Samir: We offer 6/12/24 month reserved plans. Pricing improves with longer commit and volume. Also we offer a short-term burst allowance if you need to handle unexpected peaks, as an add-on.
[06:15] Dana: Two concerns — (1) we don't want to overcommit and be stuck, (2) we need predictable monthly op-ex. Can Redwood provide an elasticity plan that smooths cost?
[06:25] Priya: Yes, hybrid: baseline reserved with a small on-demand cushion. Also, capacity smoothing via scheduled pre-warm for known windows. We can model expected monthly cost with worst/best-case traffic profiles.
[06:36] Evan: Are there cases where private is strictly required legally vs dedicated?
[06:40] Priya (SE): If your contracts require complete control of control plane, no third-party control plane metadata, or air-gapped operation, Private is the path. For most regulated needs, dedicated with strict SLAs and BYOK is sufficient, but legal should review.
[06:56] Priyanka (Security): We'll want a security workshop. GDPR data flows, retention, KMS, RBAC, SSO via SAML, and penetration test cadence.
[07:05] Samir: Absolutely, we'll set that up. I'll include the security pack and a checklist.
[07:08] Marcus: One more infra detail — does Redwood support GPU selection (A100 vs H100 vs older) for dedicated pools? We have cost sensitivity but also want consistent latency.
[07:18] Priya (SE): Yes, you can choose machine class for dedicated pools; H100s give better perf for larger models but cost more. We can model throughput per GPU class in the sizing doc.
[07:28] Dana: For the benchmark — we can supply 7 days of traces and 20 canonical prompts, plus labels for expected completions.
[07:34] Priya (SE): Perfect. That will allow us to size and run a realistic bench. We'll also include quantization experiments.
[07:41] Evan: Timeline — we want a decision in 3 weeks. Is that realistic?
[07:45] Samir: Yes. Pilot results in 2 weeks, security review in parallel, then decision meeting.
[07:51] Diego: Note: for evals we sometimes see transcribed tokens differ between quantized and fp16 models; we'll highlight where reranks or filters needed.
[07:58] Marcus: Ok, any blockers on our side? We'll need costs and the contract language for data residency and incident response.
[08:06] Samir: We'll send the basic contract excerpt and SLAs template.
[08:10] Priyanka (Security): One gotcha — if we overflow to hosted during a burst, we need to ensure no PII crosses outside permitted boundaries. How does overflow handle data segmentation?
[08:19] Priya (SE): Good callout. Overflow policies can be restricted — you can disable overflow for endpoints that touch PII, or strip sensitive context before sending to hosted. We'll document options.
[08:31] Evan: Also — do you maintain per-route cost analytics? We need to see token spend by product route.
[08:36] Samir: Redwood Console has per-route token/cost breakdowns, per-token latency percentiles, and tracing hooks you can integrate into your telemetry.
[08:45] Dana: ok let's recap next steps.
[08:47] Samir: Recap: Redwood sends pricing scenarios + TCO, security pack and SLAs; Priya sends benchmark template; Crucible shares traces and prompts; schedule security sync and follow-up on 2/22.
[08:59] Dana: sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:02] Marcus: Thank you.
[09:04] Priyanka: Thanks.
[09:07] Samir: We'll send meeting notes and action items. Bye.
[09:10] Speaker 1: (background) yeah thanks bye
